To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a clostridium species that produces a toxin that destroys motor neurons causes ALS; (2) a toxin that is produced by this species can be found in the gut of ALS patients; (3) this toxin destroys motor neurons in vitro, and (4) this toxin is not found in the gut in healthy controls.
A clostridial motor neuron toxin produced in the gut causes ALS.
